Covers 3.3 atomic radius (with one ion example, Mg vs Mg2+), 3.4 ionization energy (successive IE, aluminum) and electronegativity, 3.6 why. fields.headline:
Periodic
Trends
fields.subhead: Ionization energy, electronegativity and atomic radius, and the one idea behind all three.

alt.section: Periodic table outline with arrows across and down

fields.headline: Two Things Control Every Trend
fields.subhead: Keep both in mind. Every slide after this one uses them.
fields.c1_b:
More protons pull harder on every electron.

Across a period: one more proton each step.
fields.c2_b:
Each new level puts electrons farther out.

Down a group: one more level each step.
fields.mustwrite: More protons pull harder. More energy levels put electrons farther out.

alt.concept: Lithium and fluorine atoms: same two levels, fluorine smaller with 9 protons

fields.headline: Ionization Energy
fields.subhead: The energy needed to pull one electron off an atom, in kJ/mol.
fields.a1_b: Rises: more protons, same levels, tighter grip.
fields.a2_b: Falls: the outer electron is farther out.
fields.a3_b: Noble gases peak. Group 1 metals bottom out.

alt.diagram: First ionization energy for elements 1 to 20

fields.headline: Predict: Pulling Electrons Off Aluminum
fields.subhead: Aluminum has 3 valence electrons. Which removal costs the most?
fields.a1_b: Which bar jumps? Write your guess and why.
fields.a2_b: The 4th electron costs four times the 3rd.
fields.a3_b: Electron 4 comes from level 2: closer, less shielded.

fields.headline: Your Turn: Use the Jump
fields.subhead: Find the jump, then count the electrons before it.
fields.problem: These are magnesium's first four ionization energies. How many valence electrons does magnesium have?
fields.q2_b: 2 valence electrons. Magnesium is in group 2.
fields.answer: The jump follows the last valence electron.

fields.headline: Electronegativity
fields.subhead: How strongly an atom pulls on electrons it shares in a bond. No units.
fields.a1_b: Rises: more protons pull the shared pair harder.
fields.a2_b: Falls: the shared pair sits farther out.
fields.a3_b: IE removes an electron. EN pulls on a shared one.

alt.diagram: Electronegativity across period 2 and down group 17

fields.headline: Example: Rank by Electronegativity
fields.subhead: Use where they sit, not memorized numbers.
fields.problem: Rank oxygen, sulfur and fluorine from lowest to highest electronegativity.
fields.q1_b: S is below O: one more level, so S < O.
fields.q2_b: F is right of O: more protons, so O < F.

alt.setup: Positions of oxygen, fluorine and sulfur

fields.headline: Atomic Radius
fields.subhead: Distance from the nucleus to the outer electrons, in picometers (pm).
fields.a1_b: Shrinks: more protons pull the same levels in.
fields.a2_b: Grows: each period adds an energy level.
fields.a3_b: Radius runs opposite to IE and EN.

alt.diagram: Atoms drawn to scale across period 3 and down group 1

fields.headline: Predict: Mg vs. Mg^{2+}
fields.subhead: Magnesium loses its 2 valence electrons. Bigger, smaller or the same?
fields.a1_b: Write your guess and one reason.
fields.a2_b: 160 pm down to 72 pm: less than half.
fields.a3_b: Its outer level is gone. 12 protons hold 2 levels.

alt.diagram: Magnesium atom and magnesium ion drawn to scale

fields.headline: One Picture, Three Trends
fields.subhead: Label the arrows on your Gizmo sheet, including the diagonal.
fields.a1_b: Radius shrinks. Ionization energy and EN rise.
fields.a2_b: Radius grows. Ionization energy and EN fall.

alt.diagram: Periodic table outline with trend arrows

fields.headline: Check Yourself
fields.subhead: Answer in your notes first. Then we click through.
fields.problem: Calcium and bromine are both in period 4. Which atom is larger? Which has the higher ionization energy?
fields.q1_b: Calcium. Bromine has 15 more protons on 4 levels.
fields.q2_b: Bromine. More protons grip its electrons tighter.
fields.answer: Same cause: more protons, same levels.
